chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him, "If some event occurs, and Allah does not show me that, then whom should I follow as Imam?" So he gestured toward his son Mūsā.
He said: I said, "Then if an event happens to Mūsā, whom should I follow as Imam?" He said, "His son."
I said, "Then if an event happens to his son, and he leaves behind an elder brother and a young son, then whom should I follow as Imam?" He said, "His son, then one after another."
And in the copy of al-Ṣafwānī: "Then it is like this forever."

key_terms.أَئْتَمُّ: to take someone as Imam and follow his authority
key_terms.بِوَلَدِهِ: through his son; indicating succession to the son
key_terms.مُوسَى: Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, identified here as the next Imam
key_terms.وَاحِدًا فَوَاحِدًا: one after another in continuous succession

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the continuation of the Imamate among the descendants of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imamate continues through the descendant of the Imam, passing from son to son in succession. It also clarifies that the authority does not return to an elder brother when a son is present, affirming hereditary continuity within the designated line of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ibn Abu Najran, 
(It has been narrated) from Isa Bin Abdullah Bin Umar Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘If what is to happen does happen, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> not Show me (that), so with whom should I take as an Imam<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> gestured towards his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So if is an event (of death) occurs with Musa<sup>asws</sup>, so with whom shall I take as an Imam<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>’.

I said, ‘So if an event (of death) occurs with his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> leaves a lot of brothers, or young sons, so with whom shall I take as an Imam<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>, then one after one’.
And in a copy of Al-Safwany, (He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘Then it would be like this, forever!’
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ibn abu Najran from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abdallah ibn ‘Umar ibn Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) who has said that he asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) the following.
“Would there happen what is to happen, may Allah would not show me such a day (death of the Imam (a.s.) who then must I follow as my Imam?” The Imam (a.s.) pointed to his son Musa (a.s.).
The narrator has said that he asked the Imams (a.s.), “ What if something will happen to Musa (a.s.) who then must I follow?” The Imam (a.s.), “Follow a son.”

I then asked, “What if something would happen to the son and the Imam would leave behind an elder brother or a small son then who must I follow?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Follow his son and so on one after the other.”
In the script of Sawan it says, “. .and so on forever.”
